{{< include _elements-kit.qmd >}}

**Texture** is how many layers of sound there are and how they relate to each other. Thin or thick is part of it, but the
names below describe the *relationship* between the parts.

Almost every example on this page uses the same tune (*Twinkle, Twinkle*), so you hear only the texture change.

## 1. Monophonic

One line, and nothing else. Any number of people can play or sing it, as long as they all play the same part.
No chords.

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="96"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Monophonic
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
G G d d|e e d2|c c B B|A A G2|]
</script></div>

## 2. Octaves

Two or more parts playing the same tune an **octave** apart: the same note names at a different pitch. Still one line,
but heavier.

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="96"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:In octaves
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
[G,G] [G,G] [Dd] [Dd]|[Ee] [Ee] [Dd]2|[Cc] [Cc] [B,B] [B,B]|[A,A] [A,A] [G,G]2|]
</script></div>

## 3. Homophonic

All the parts move **together, in the same rhythm**, making chords, like a hymn. (*Homo-phonic* = "same sound".)

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="80"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Homophonic: four parts, one rhythm
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
V:1
G G d d|e e d2|c c B B|A A G2|]
V:2
D D G G|G G F2|E E D G|G F D2|]
V:3 clef=bass
B, B, B, B,|C C A,2|G, A, G, D|E D B,2|]
V:4 clef=bass
G, G, G, G,|C, C, D,2|E, C, G, G,|C, D, G,,2|]
</script></div>

## 4. Melody and accompaniment

A tune with chords or a pattern underneath that supports it. The most common texture in pop music and Classical-period
music. An **Alberti bass** is a Classical piano accompaniment: each chord broken into four equal notes, usually lowest,
highest, middle, highest.

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Melody over an Alberti bass
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
V:1
G G d d|e e d2|c c B B|A A G2|]
V:2 clef=bass
L:1/8
G,DB,D G,DB,D|C,G,E,G, G,DB,D|A,,E,C,E, G,DB,D|D,A,F,A, G,DB,D|]
</script></div>

## 5. Polyphonic

Two or more **independent** lines at once, each a tune in its own right (*poly-phonic* = "many sounds"). Also called
**counterpoint**. When the lines copy each other it is **imitation**; a **round** (*Frère Jacques*) and a **canon** are
strict imitation.

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="96"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Polyphonic: Frère Jacques as a round, the second voice two measures behind
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
V:1
G A B G|G A B G|B c d2|B c d2|
V:2
z4|z4|G A B G|G A B G|]
</script></div>

A **countermelody** is a second tune that fits with the main one, as in a descant over a hymn.

## 6. Call and response, antiphonal

**Call and response**: one performer (or group) plays or sings a phrase, and another answers. Common in African music,
blues, gospel, work songs and pop.

**Antiphonal**: two groups answering each other from **different places**, such as two choirs on either side of a church.

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="104"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:Call (top) and response (bottom)
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
V:1
G G d d|z4|c c B B|z4|]
V:2 clef=bass
z4|E, E, D,2|z4|A,, A,, G,,2|]
</script></div>

## 7. Pedal and drone

A **pedal** is a long or repeated note, usually in the bass, held while the harmony changes above it. A **drone** is long
or repeated notes, usually two a 5th apart, as on bagpipes.

<div class="abc-ex" data-bpm="96"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
T:The tune over a drone on G and D
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:G
V:1
G G d d|e e d2|c c B B|A A G2|]
V:2 clef=bass
[G,,D,]4|[G,,D,]4|[G,,D,]4|[G,,D,]4|]
</script></div>

## 8. Basso continuo

In the Baroque period, the **basso continuo** played the bass line and filled in the chords under the melody. The bass
was played by a cello, bass viol or bassoon; the chords by a harpsichord, organ or lute, read from a **figured bass**
(numbers under the bass notes showing the chords).

## 9. Describing texture

- Name it, then describe it: *thin* or *thick*, *sparse* or *dense*, how many parts.
- Say what changes: "It starts **monophonic** (a solo flute), becomes **homophonic** when the choir comes in, and the
  middle section is **polyphonic**, with the voices entering one after another in **imitation**."
- Which instruments have the melody and which accompany: see [Instruments and Voices](elements-instruments.qmd#what-is-each-instrument-doing).
